description: WU-9T (leafblower-2ouc.17): pre-registered per-competitor hyperparameter table. Per DESIGN.md Section 5 each entry records the package's DOCUMENTED / RECOMMENDED (not leafblower-tuned) native hyperparameters -- convergence tolerance (and the QUANTITY it bounds), max iterations, entropic epsilon, OSQP/scipy solver tolerances -- WITH a citation URL and the package version the value applies to (WU-10 installed versions). This table is git-FROZEN before the WU-REH rehearsal (Blocker C): any change after freeze is a disclosed, re-tagged, re-rehearsed amendment. Keys are the registry ids from benchmarks/study/registry.json (WU-10). leafblower's OWN solvers are NOT here -- their tol->native-param mapping lives in tol_mapping.json. Values were researched directly from official CRAN man pages / vignettes / package source / readthedocs (WebSearch+WebFetch, 2026-07-08/09), NOT via agy and NOT invented. Where a package's documented default could not be confirmed from primary docs the entry records null + a 'flag' note rather than a guess.

provenance.method: direct WebSearch + WebFetch of official CRAN man pages (rdrr.io, cran.r-project.org, package pkgdown sites), package source (GitHub raw), and readthedocs (POT, ott-jax, scipy, cvxpy); no agy delegation this session (session override).
provenance.versions_source: WU-10 installed-version list (freeze against these exact versions).

survey_calibrate_raking.convergence_bounds_quantity: epsilon = max allowed absolute value of (population total - calibration estimate) matched population total; Newton-Raphson iteration cap = maxit.
survey_calibrate_raking.citation: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survey/survey.pdf (calibrate.survey.design2 signature: maxit=50, epsilon=1e-7, verbose=FALSE, force=FALSE); engine grake().
survey_calibrate_raking.note: Raking calfun. Defaults documented/recommended, not tuned.

survey_calibrate_linear.convergence_bounds_quantity: epsilon = absolute tolerance on |population total - estimate|. Unbounded linear calibration is a direct linear solve (maxit/epsilon still meaningful for bounded/collinear fallback).

params.bounds: REQUIRED (Deville-Sarndal L<1<U; no default) -- benchmark supplies per-problem [min,max]

survey_calibrate_logit.convergence_bounds_quantity: epsilon = absolute tolerance on |population total - estimate|; logit distance is the bounded Deville-Sarndal g-weight function.
survey_calibrate_logit.note: Bounds are mandatory for logit and are set from the problem spec, not a package default.

sampling_calib_linear.convergence_bounds_quantity: Linear method is a closed-form g-weight solve; max_iter (default 500) applies only to the iterative methods (raking/truncated/logit). Convergence checked via checkcalibration on |X'w - total|.

params.bounds: c(low=0, upp=10) [package default; benchmark overrides per problem]

sampling_calib_logit.convergence_bounds_quantity: Iterative Newton on the bounded logit distance; max_iter=500 iteration cap. g-weights constrained to [low,upp].
sampling_calib_logit.note: bounds default c(0,10); benchmark passes per-problem bounds.

anesrake.convergence_bounds_quantity: convcrit = 0.01 stopping change threshold; maxit=1000 iteration cap; cap=5 caps weight ratio (design-weight multiple). type/pctlim/nlim/choosemethod govern which margins enter raking (ANES variable selection).
anesrake.citation: https://github.com/cran/anesrake/blob/master/R/anesrake.R (signature: weightvec=NULL, cap=5, verbose=FALSE, maxit=1000, type='pctlim', pctlim=5, nlim=5, choosemethod='total', iterate=TRUE, convcrit=0.01, force1=TRUE).

ipfr.convergence_bounds_quantity: max_iterations=30 iteration cap over the list-balancing/IPU sweeps; min_weight floors cell weights (aids convergence). Convergence measured on % gap to targets. min_ratio/max_ratio cap weight extremity (off by default => null).
ipfr.note: Documented convergence-tolerance scalar not exposed as a named arg; controlled via max_iterations + min_weight per vignette.

ebal.convergence_bounds_quantity: constraint.tolerance=1 => converged when max(abs(covariate-moment gradient co.x.agg - tr.total)) < 1 (absolute count-scale imbalance on expanded moment constraints); max.iterations=200 Newton cap. base.weight NULL => uniform.
ebal.citation: https://rdrr.io/cran/ebal/man/ebalance.html (ebalance(Treatment, X, base.weight=NULL, ..., max.iterations=200, constraint.tolerance=1, print.level=0)); solver in R/eb.R.
ebal.note: Entropy balancing (Hainmueller 2012). constraint.tolerance is on the RAW moment (count) scale, not a proportion -- record as the documented default (1).

optweight_entropy.convergence_bounds_quantity: tols=0 => EXACT balance (weighted mean within 0 of target per covariate); min.w=1e-8 weight floor. Solver-level convergence handed to the QP/conic backend (OSQP defaults).
optweight_entropy.citation: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/optweight/optweight.pdf and vignette https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/optweight/vignettes/optweight.html (optweight(..., tols=0, norm='l2', min.w=1e-08, ...); norm='entropy' = relative-entropy objective).
optweight_entropy.note: norm set to 'entropy' for the ORIS_soft family. tols=0 = documented default (exact balance).

params.solver: osqp (REQUIRED for linf if highs absent)

optweight_linf.convergence_bounds_quantity: tols=0 exact balance; minimax (L-infinity) weight-dispersion objective solved via OSQP. Reported OSQP tolerances are the OSQP package defaults (optweight does not document overriding them).
optweight_linf.citation: optweight man/vignette (norm='linf' requires osqp) https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/optweight/optweight.pdf ; OSQP defaults https://osqp.org/docs/interfaces/solver_settings.html (eps_abs=1e-3, eps_rel=1e-3, max_iter=4000).
optweight_linf.note: OSQP eps values are the SOLVER defaults, cited separately; optweight itself documents no override => recorded as backend default, flag if driver tightens.

sbw.convergence_bounds_quantity: No scalar convergence tolerance: bal_alg=TRUE runs an ALGORITHMIC search over the bal_gri tolerance grid (default c(1e-4..0.1)) for the tightest feasible standardized balance tolerance; the QP is solved by sol_nam ('osqp'). bal_tol bounds standardized covariate imbalance. osqp settings are HARDCODED inside sbw (.sbwpriosqp: eps_prim_inf=eps_dual_inf=1e-32, alpha=1, polish=TRUE); eps_abs/eps_rel/max_iter are NOT forwarded via the sol list, so solve accuracy is osqp-default+polish (untunable through sbw's public API). osqp exposes out$status ('solved' => converged).
sbw.citation: https://rdrr.io/cran/sbw/man/sbw.html (sbw(..., bal=list(bal_alg=TRUE, bal_tol, bal_std='group', bal_gri=c(1e-04,0.001,0.002,0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1), bal_sam=1000), sol=list(sol_nam='osqp', sol_dis=FALSE), par=list(par_est='att'))).
sbw.note: Stable Balancing Weights (Zubizarreta 2015). Documented default is the tolerance GRID + algorithmic search, not a single tol. AMENDMENT (config-freeze-v4, 2026-07-09): sol_nam quadprog->osqp. quadprog is a DENSE active-set QP (O(n_control^2) Hessian) infeasible on the stepstone (1.58M rows) and hangs by n_control~2e4; osqp is sbw's sparse-ADMM free CRAN backend that scales and (via sbw's hardcoded polish=TRUE) returns the same QP optimum (cor 0.9999, max|dw|~1e-4). Free alternatives rejected: quadprog dead-at-scale; pogs not-on-CRAN + abandoned(~2017) + broken Linux build => not reproducible. No commercial (gurobi/mosek/cplex) per free-only reproducibility constraint.

params.method: delegated (ebal / optweight for the calibration families)

weightit.convergence_bounds_quantity: WeightIt is a WRAPPER: convergence tolerance / iteration cap are those of the delegated engine (e.g. method='ebal' -> ebal-style entropy-balancing solver; method='optweight' -> optweight/OSQP). WeightIt documents no single package-wide calibration tolerance default.
weightit.note: FLAG: no package-level documented calibration tolerance/iteration default -- delegated to the chosen method's engine. Driver (WU-5) must record which method WeightIt is invoked with and inherit that engine's frozen entry (ebal / optweight above).

icarus.convergence_bounds_quantity: calibTolerance=1e-6 = tolerance on the max relative margin gap; maxIter=2500 iteration cap. method in {linear, raking, logit, truncated}; logit/truncated use bounds.

laeken.convergence_bounds_quantity: tol=1e-6 = convergence tolerance on the calibration constraint match; maxit=500 iteration cap; bounds c(0,10) constrain g-weights (used by logit); eps = numerical tolerance for singularity handling.
laeken.citation: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/laeken/html/calibWeights.html (calibWeights(X, d, totals, ..., bounds=c(0,10), maxit=500, tol=1e-06, eps=.Machine$double.eps)).

gecal.entrypoint: GECal::GEcalib(formula, dweight, data, const, method=..., entropy=..., ...)
gecal.convergence_bounds_quantity: xtol=1e-16 = relative steplength tolerance in the nleqslv nonlinear solver; maxit=1e5 major-iteration cap. method in {GEC,GEC0,DS}; entropy in {SL,EL,ET,CE,HD,PH} (SL=squared-loss default => chi2-like; ET=exp-tilting => raking; CE => logit-like).
gecal.citation: https://rdrr.io/cran/GECal/man/GEcalib.html (GEcalib(formula, dweight, data=NULL, const, method=c('GEC','GEC0','DS'), entropy=c('SL','EL','ET','CE','HD','PH'), weight.scale=1, G.scale=1, K_alpha=NULL, is.total=TRUE, del=NULL, xtol=1e-16, maxit=1e+05, allowSingular=T)).
gecal.note: Unifying generalized-entropy baseline (Kwon-Kim-Qiu 2024). Solver = nleqslv; documented defaults.

jointcalib.convergence_bounds_quantity: control_calib: tol=1e-8 convergence tolerance on the calibration constraint; maxit=50 iteration cap; bounds c(0,10) for bounded methods. joint_calib calibrates on totals + quantiles (Harms-Duchesne 2006).
jointcalib.note: Newton-KL / TR-dual analog family. Documented control_calib defaults.

nonprobsvy.convergence_bounds_quantity: control_sel(est_method='gee'): the Chen-Li-Wu calibration-constraint dual solved by nleqslv with global strategy 'dbldog' (double-dogleg trust region) = the closest Newton-KL/TR-dual analog per DESIGN.md Section 2 line 71. epsilon=1e-4 convergence tolerance on the estimating equations; maxit=500 cap; gee_h_fun=1. NOTE: est_method was corrected from 'mle' -> 'gee' (WU-5b, 2026-07-09): the 'mle' propensity-MLE (maxLik/NR/BFGS) path is Newton-Raphson on the selection model, NOT the TR-dual this competitor's registry slot requires; the descriptive text already named GEE as the intended analog, so the params block was the authoring error.
nonprobsvy.note: FLAG-minor: docs also reference 1e-6 in narrative; signature default recorded (epsilon=1e-4). Driver should assert the installed-version signature.

regenesees.convergence_bounds_quantity: epsilon=1e-7 = max allowed absolute relative difference between population totals and calibrated estimates; maxit=50 Newton-Raphson cap; bounds on weight/direct-weight ratio (default unbounded). Unbounded linear = direct solve.

params.role: reference / ground-truth anchor (NOT a competitor to rank)

cvxr_reference.convergence_bounds_quantity: Interior-point duality-gap / feasibility tolerances (abstol/reltol/feastol). Per DESIGN.md Section 6 the reference solve is deliberately TIGHTENED to ~1e-12 to serve as the RQ5 correctness anchor -- this is a design-of-record recommended value, NOT the package default (default is 1e-8).
cvxr_reference.citation: CVXR psolve / solver-parameters docs https://www.cvxgrp.org/CVXR/reference/psolve.html and https://cvxr.rbind.io/cvxr_examples/cvxr_solver-parameters/ (feastol/reltol/abstol, default ~1e-8); tightening to 1e-12 per DESIGN.md Section 6.
cvxr_reference.note: Reference anchor, not a ranked competitor. The 1e-12 target is a documented DESIGN-of-record choice; the 1e-8 figures are the ECOS package defaults.

ipfn.convergence_bounds_quantity: convergence_rate=1e-5 = stop when max relative marginal error < this; max_iteration=500 cap; rate_tolerance=1e-8 = stop when |conv - old_conv| < this (stalled progress). Bounds the proportional-fitting marginal error.

weightipy.convergence_bounds_quantity: convcrit=0.01 = convergence criterion (stop when relative error-reduction pct_still = 1-convcrit is reached); max_iterations=1000 cap. RIM/iterative raking marginal error. cap off by default.
weightipy.note: Maintained Quantipy3 RIM fork. Documented source defaults.

params.reg: REQUIRED entropic regularization epsilon (no default) -- benchmark pins per problem (see note)

pot_sinkhorn.convergence_bounds_quantity: stopThr=1e-9 = stop threshold on the marginal error (transport-plan row/col constraint violation); numItermax=1000 cap. reg = entropic epsilon (mandatory positional; POT gives NO default). Recommended epsilon range in POT tutorials is problem-scaled (typically 1e-3 to 1e-1 x median cost); benchmark documents the pinned value in the OT-reduction spec.
pot_sinkhorn.note: 2-marginal balanced OT (redundant-IPF cross-check only, per DESIGN Section 2). reg has NO documented default => the epsilon value is a per-spec pinned choice, recorded in the OT-reduction spec, not here.

pot_greenkhorn.convergence_bounds_quantity: stopThr=1e-9 marginal-error stop threshold; numItermax=10000 cap (greedy coordinate updates, hence higher cap than sinkhorn). reg = entropic epsilon (mandatory, no default).
pot_greenkhorn.note: Greedy Sinkhorn variant. reg has no documented default (per-spec pinned).

params.epsilon: geometry-relative default (~5% of mean cost; set via Geometry, no scalar Sinkhorn default)

ott_jax_sinkhorn.convergence_bounds_quantity: threshold=1e-3 = tolerance to stop Sinkhorn iterations (marginal deviation); max_iterations=2000 cap; error recomputed every inner_iterations=10; min_iterations=0. epsilon = entropic regularization on the Geometry (relative-to-mean-cost default).
ott_jax_sinkhorn.note: EXCLUDED from ranked {1,4}-thread timing (XLA ignores OMP/BLAS env; DESIGN Section 2). epsilon set on Geometry, not the solver; scalar Geometry default is relative (~0.05 x mean cost).

scipy_trust_constr.convergence_bounds_quantity: gtol=1e-8 = stop on Lagrangian-gradient (first-order KKT / dual-stationarity) infinity norm; xtol=1e-8 = trust-region step tolerance; barrier_tol=1e-8 = interior-point barrier tolerance; maxiter=1000 cap. Newton-KL trust-region analog.
scipy_trust_constr.citation: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/optimize.minimize-trustconstr.html (gtol default 1e-8, xtol default 1e-8, barrier_tol default 1e-8, maxiter default 1000).

params.default_solver: CLARABEL (CVXPY default for LP/SOCP since v1.5)

cvxpy_linf.convergence_bounds_quantity: CLARABEL interior-point tolerances: tol_gap_abs/tol_gap_rel = duality-gap tolerances; tol_feas = primal/dual feasibility tolerance; max_iter=200 cap. Bounds the LP minimax (L-infinity) optimality/feasibility gap.
cvxpy_linf.citation: https://www.cvxpy.org/tutorial/solvers/index.html (CLARABEL default since 1.5); CLARABEL default settings tol_gap_abs=1e-8, tol_gap_rel=1e-8, tol_feas=1e-8, max_iter=200 (https://clarabel.org/stable/api_settings/).
cvxpy_linf.note: L-infinity LP baseline (DESIGN Section 2, RQ6 item 2). CLARABEL defaults recorded; if the driver forces a specific solver (ECOS/OSQP) that entry's defaults apply instead -- flag on driver wiring.

balance.convergence_bounds_quantity: balance.rake wraps the ipfn IPF backend; the marginal-error convergence semantics are ipfn's (see ipfn entry). balance's own rake wrapper forwards max_iteration/convergence_rate/rate_tolerance to ipfn.
balance.citation: https://import-balance.org/ and https://github.com/facebookresearch/balance (rake adjustment uses ipfn backend); ipfn defaults per the ipfn entry.
balance.note: FLAG: balance's public rake() wrapper does not document its OWN numeric convergence defaults distinctly from the ipfn backend it calls -- recorded null. Driver (WU-6) must capture the effective forwarded values at call time; treat as ipfn defaults (convergence_rate=1e-5, max_iteration=500, rate_tolerance=1e-8) unless balance overrides them.

samplics.convergence_bounds_quantity: Raking iterates until margins agree 'within tolerance' (JOSS paper), but samplics' public API does not surface a documented numeric default tolerance / max-iteration for its calibration in the primary docs.
samplics.citation: https://samplics-org.github.io/samplics/ (calibration/raking described; no numeric default surfaced). Successor 'svy' documents rake tol=1e-6 (https://svylab.com/docs/svy/tutorials/weighting.html).
samplics.note: FLAG: documented numeric default unknown for samplics 0.6.0 -- recorded null. Its successor svy uses tol=1e-6 (see svy entry); driver (WU-6, external-review Gap E) verifies which library is actually used and records the effective value.

svy.entrypoint: svy rake(controls, wgt_name, tol=...) / svy calibrate(controls, ...)
svy.convergence_bounds_quantity: rake tol=1e-6 = tolerance on the raking marginal match; calibrate() and the numeric max-iterations default are documented only via TrimConfig ('convergence tolerance, maximum iterations') without stated numeric defaults.
svy.citation: https://svylab.com/docs/svy/tutorials/weighting.html (rake(..., tol=1e-6); calibrate(...); TrimConfig bundles tolerance/max-iterations without numeric defaults).
svy.note: Confirmed maintained samplics successor (svylab.com) -- resolves DESIGN Section 2 Gap E. rake tol=1e-6 documented; FLAG: calibrate/max-iterations numeric defaults not documented (null).
